memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Every animal that does not have a divided hoof or that does not chew the cud is unclean for you; whoever touches the carcass of any of them will be unclean. Of all the animals that walk on all fours, those that walk on their paws are unclean for you; whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean till evening. Anyone who picks up their carcasses must wash their clothes, and they will be unclean till evening. They are unclean for you." - Lev 11:26-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These verses cover the animals people actually lived with — the ones that walk on paws, the ones found dead on a path, the ones a shepherd or a child might stumble across on any given day.

That is the point. God's instructions were not written for a temple ceremony once a year. They were written for Tuesday. For the man walking home. For the woman washing clothes. For the boy who touched something he should not have.

We often keep our faith in a compartment. Church on Sunday, Bible in the morning, and then a long stretch of ordinary hours where we assume God is not particularly involved. Leviticus refuses that division. The God of Israel followed His people out of the tabernacle and into the fields, the kitchens, and the washing lines.

Paul says the same thing in a single sentence: whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all for the glory of God (1 Cor 10:31). Not just the religious parts. All of it.

Your commute is worship. Your work is worship. The way you handle a frustrating afternoon is worship. God is not waiting for you at church next Sunday — He is with you right now, in the middle of the ordinary.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which parts of your week do you unconsciously treat as "outside" your walk with God?
2. How would today look different if you saw it as an offering to God?
3. What is one ordinary task you could deliberately do for God's glory today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for keeping You in a corner of my week. Walk with me through the ordinary hours, and let my whole life — not just the religious parts — be an offering to You. Amen.
